clue.text: Wife tucking into Danish swirl (cold packaged snack)

indicators.note: the wife is tucked inside the shuffled letters, like a filling
to swirl is to whirl round, so the letters of Danish, with the cold letter packaged among them, are churned into a new order

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies

explanation.surface: A wife digging into a Danish pastry while wrapped up for a cold packed lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packaged' looks like it describes the snack; it says the cold letter is wrapped in among the swirled letters, before the wife is tucked in.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandwich is the classic light meal of bread and filling eaten between meals.

clue.text: Most cunning second lieutenant definitely captured

indicators.note: captured means taken prisoner, so the officer letters hold the affirmative inside

parts.note: yes, definitely: an emphatic agreement

explanation.surface: A wily junior officer has certainly been taken prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second lieutenant' reads as a single rank but splits into two abbreviations, with the affirmative put between L and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Sly means cunning or crafty, so slyest is the superlative, most crafty.

clue.text: In Tijuana, chose an accompaniment for 9

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits within the words Tijuana, chose

explanation.surface: Someone in a Mexican border town orders a side dish to go with chilli.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is CHILLI CON CARNE; the answer is in tijuaNA CHOSe.
explanation.definitionFit: Nachos, tortilla chips, are a Tex-Mex side often served with chilli con carne.

clue.text: Perhaps duck Buddhist temple flower arrangement

parts.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia

indicators.note: a flower arrangement suggests the letters of flower are themselves arranged anew

explanation.surface: Floral displays decorating a Buddhist temple, perhaps with a duck nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower arrangement' reads as floristry but 'arrangement' rearranges FLOWER into ERFOWL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks are an example of waterfowl, birds that live on water; 'Perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: "The Art of Film-making" broadcast March 16 receiving Oscar

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so all these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 16 down is EGYPTIAN
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A documentary on filmmaking is screened in March, picking up an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scrambles MARCH, EGYPTIAN (16) and O together; 'receiving' just adds O to the pool. 'Oscar' looks like the film award, but is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinematography is the craft of lighting and shooting moving pictures, central to making films.

clue.text: Madame securing laboratory, about to prepare cadaver

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole assembled string is read backwards
securing means holding something inside, so Madame's letters enclose the laboratory

explanation.surface: A French madame takes over a lab, ready to work on a dead body, like a mortician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole assembled string backwards, not just the laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: To embalm is to treat a corpse with preservatives, which is how a cadaver is prepared for burial or display.

clue.text: Object reportedly dug out of the ground

indicators.note: reportedly means as said or heard, so the answer sounds like the word for object

parts.note: to mind is to object, as in do you mind?

explanation.surface: An object said to have been unearthed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun, but is the verb: MIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Mined describes coal or ore that has been extracted from beneath the earth.

clue.text: American boy band serving up first class delicious food

parts.note: Bros was a British boy band of the late 1980s

indicators.note: serving up in a down clue means placing the letters upwards, so first class is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first class, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: An American pop group dishes up fine cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: Bros were a British boy band of the late 1980s. 'serving up' turns AI backwards to give IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods, now any delicious food.

clue.text: Measure of explosion's size worrying to gasmen

indicators.note: worrying means troubling or shaking, so the letters of to gasmen are shaken up

explanation.surface: The scale of a gas explosion is a source of anxiety to gas engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worrying' rearranges TO GASMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaton is a unit of explosive force equal to a million tons of TNT, used for nuclear yields.

clue.text: I say; got a cold nose Mr Schwarzenegger? This'll warm you up!

indicators.note: I say flags that the phrase is to be spoken, giving the answer by its sound

parts.words: got a cold nose Mr Schwarzenegger
parts.note: chilly conk Arnie: chilly is cold, conk is British slang for nose, and Arnie is Arnold Schwarzenegger

explanation.surface: Someone asks Arnold Schwarzenegger if his nose is cold, then offers something to warm him.
explanation.walkthrough: Conk is British slang for nose; Arnie is Schwarzenegger's nickname. Said aloud, chilly conk, Arnie? matches the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli con carne is a spicy dish of meat and beans; its heat and chilli warm the eater.

clue.text: By gum! Coal trains regularly left Gulf state

indicators.note: taking letters regularly, every other one, from the run By gum Coal trains, skipping the first and keeping the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A northern exclamation as the coal trains pull out of a station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum!' looks like a stray exclamation but its letters are part of the stretch picked from; 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th letters onwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Yucatán is a Mexican state on the peninsula of the same name, bordering the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: On board, Turkish and BA grant one small item of luggage

indicators.note: on board means carried within, so the answer travels inside the words Turkish and BA grant

explanation.surface: Turkish Airlines and British Airways each allow a passenger one small piece of cabin baggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' signals letters carried inside the airline names: turkisH AND BAG rant.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbag is a small bag carried by hand, the one personal item airlines let you bring aboard.

clue.text: Out of time, soldiers reverse track

indicators.note: reverse here instructs reading the remaining letters backwards
out of means without, so the time letter is removed from the soldiers

parts.note: troops are soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers who have run out of time pull back and retrace their path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' takes T from TROOPS to leave ROOPS; 'reverse' turns that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the trail of footprints or droppings left by an animal, which hunters follow as a track.

clue.text: Clumsy mother and boy run riot

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
a lad is a boy

indicators.note: run here is a verb telling the letters of riot to run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A mother and her son go on a rampage, knocking everything over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' looks like part of the phrase 'run riot' but is the anagram signal turning RIOT into ROIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit is a formal word for awkward or lacking dexterity, the opposite of adroit.

clue.text: Waste our bitcoin acquiring new Time subscription

indicators.note: acquiring means taking in, so the shuffled letters take in the two abbreviations
to waste is to wreck, so the letters of our bitcoin are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Squander our cryptocurrency on a magazine subscription to Time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste' rearranges OUR BITCOIN into CORIBUTION; 'acquiring' puts N and T inside after CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A subscription is a sum paid into a fund or society, which is one sense of a contribution.

clue.text: Poor student eating shell of langoustine hasn't been paid

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so the shuffled letters take in the shellfish's outer letters
poor means badly made, so the letters of student are rearranged
shell means outer covering, so only the first and last letters of langoustine

explanation.surface: A broke student eating expensive seafood has left the bill unsettled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor student' reads as one figure, but 'Poor' is the anagram signal, giving UNSETTD, which takes the shell letters in before the D.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsettled bill or account is outstanding, still owing, not yet paid off.

clue.text: African beginning to experience pain ain't having surgery

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of experience is used

parts.note: gyp is British informal for pain, as in my knee is giving me gyp

indicators.note: having surgery means being cut and rearranged, so the letters of ain't are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone going in for an operation is just starting to feel pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Gyp is British slang for pain. 'having surgery' reorders AINT to TIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Egyptian comes from Egypt, a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Feeling rough, though apparently on course to deal with it OK!

definitions.text: apparently on course to deal with it OK
definitions.meaning: in golf, being ... on a course means taking fewer strokes than standard, so doing well; with rough also a golf term

explanation.surface: Someone is under the weather but seems to be coping.
explanation.walkthrough: Rough is also the long grass beside a golf fairway, and being below par on a golf course is good, the opposite of the everyday sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Below par means unwell, below one's usual standard; in golf it means fewer strokes than expected.

clue.text: Grizzled convict goes crazy over stuffed bird

parts.note: grizzled hair is grey
a lag, or old lag, is British slang for a convict

indicators.note: the over letter is stuffed into the jumbled letters, like a filling
crazy means mad or deranged, so the letters of goes are jumbled

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A grey-haired prisoner loses his mind over a taxidermied bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges GOES to GOSE; 'stuffed' puts O inside it to make GOOSE. 'stuffed bird' looks like the definition, but 'stuffed' is working.
explanation.definitionFit: The greylag is a large grey wild goose, the ancestor of most farmyard geese.

clue.text: Spanish mag featuring topless policewoman is fair game

indicators.note: featuring means including, so the magazine contains the trimmed officer

parts.note: ¡Hola! is a Spanish celebrity magazine, sister of Hello!

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, the first letter

parts.note: a cop is a police officer

explanation.surface: A Spanish gossip magazine runs a topless photo of a policewoman, and she is fair game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes C from COP to give OP; 'featuring' puts it in HOLA. 'fair game' sounds like a target, but is a fairground game.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoopla is a fairground game where rings are thrown over prizes.

clue.text: Cut of meat infused with a dash of rum; a dash, barely

indicators.note: infused with means having something soaked inside, so the meat holds the letter

parts.note: a steak is a cut of meat

indicators.note: a dash of means a small amount, here just the first letter of rum

explanation.surface: A recipe for steak marinated with a splash of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a dash, barely' is a cryptic definition: a dash made bare, naked.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to run naked through a public place, a dash done barely clothed.

clue.text: Instruction to reader left English grad in charge of 16 scientist

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, is printed at the foot of a page to tell the reader to go on
an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A note tells the reader an English graduate is in charge of an Egyptian scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is EGYPTIAN: Ptolemy was an astronomer of Roman Egypt, and Ptolemaic describes his earth-centred system.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptolemaic means belonging to Ptolemy, the Alexandrian astronomer, so it describes the Egyptian scientist's work.

clue.text: Breaking news from NZ: sounds like horned beast running wild

indicators.note: from means taken away from, so the news is removed from the spoken country
sounds like means the country name is read as it is spoken

parts.note: NZ is the abbreviation for New Zealand
breaking news is simply news

explanation.surface: A news flash from New Zealand about a horned animal on the loose.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, NEW ZEALAND sounds like NEWS ELAND; take the news away.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiralled horns.

clue.text: Uranium found in red freshwater fish

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside, so the uranium symbol goes within the red

parts.note: a Trot, short for Trotskyist, is a left-winger, a red
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Radioactive uranium turns up inside a red fish from a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' looks like the fish's colour but is a political label: TROT, a Trotskyist.
explanation.definitionFit: The trout is a game fish of rivers and lakes, a member of the salmon family.

clue.text: What UK constituencies have to prosecute?

parts.note: each UK constituency elects one Member of Parliament: one MP each

explanation.surface: A question about British parliamentary seats, then a call to take someone to court.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as I MP EACH: the Roman numeral I for one, MP, each.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is to bring a formal charge against an official, putting them on trial.

clue.text: 'e's looking more pasty having suffered a setback/deterioration

indicators.note: a setback sends something backwards, so the assembled letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a Cockney he's, with the h dropped, gives the letters ES
looking more pasty means paler in complexion

explanation.surface: A Cockney patient looks paler than before, having taken a turn for the worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' looks like part of the definition, but it signals the reversal; the slash then offers the definition proper.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a falling back into illness after apparent recovery, a worsening of the condition.

clue.text: S American poet Peru quietly expelled bound by gagging order

indicators.note: bound by means held inside, so the gagging order encloses the trimmed country

parts.note: an NDA, non-disclosure agreement, legally gags the signer

indicators.note: expelled means thrown out, so the quiet letter is removed from Peru

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quietly

explanation.surface: Peru throws someone out under a gagging order, keeping things hush-hush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quietly' is the musical P (piano), which 'expelled' removes from the country, leaving ERU.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Neruda was a Chilean poet who won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1971.

clue.text: Further education journalist returned criticism

parts.note: FE is the abbreviation for further education, British post-school colleges
ED, editor, is a journalist
back means returned, as in be back

explanation.surface: A college journalist comes back with critical comments.
explanation.walkthrough: FE, further education, is British schooling after 16 at a college rather than university.
explanation.definitionFit: Feedback is evaluative comment on someone's work, often critical in either direction.
